subject: Architecture
title: Arctic Architecture: Building on Melting Ground
description: A fast breakdown of Arctic Architecture: Building on Melting Ground for builders.

hook.text: In Siberia, buildings are sinking because the permafrost they sit on is melting — turning solid ground to mud.

buildup.text: Arctic buildings traditionally stand on stilts — keeping heated floors away from frozen ground to prevent melting.

discovery.text: Climate change is thawing permafrost that has been frozen for thousands of years — foundations are crumbling.

twist.text: Russia's city of Norilsk has lost 60% of its buildings to permafrost damage — entire neighborhoods are condemned.

climax.text: Engineers are testing thermosyphons — pipes that pump cold air underground to refreeze the ground beneath buildings.

punchline.text: We built on ice and called it ground. Now the ground is leaving.

quiz.question: Why are buildings in Siberian cities sinking?
options: Underground mining operations hollowed out the ground
Climate change is melting the permafrost foundations
Flooding from rivers is eroding the soil beneath them
